New 2026-09-12 -- exercises this project's Militia quality tier for the first time (previously defined in quality/tiers.py but never used by any roster row; militia's own multipliers are an uncalibrated extrapolation, see formulas.py comment). Militia classification is an EXPLICIT INFERENCE, not a sourced historian's classification -- no source found rates Home Guard quality directly; the classification rests on structural/doctrinal facts (units confined by doctrine to static local defense, not expected to join mobile field-army operations; a 1942 National Service Act provision allowing compulsory enrolment of men aged 42-51 to fill under-strength units) rather than a stated quality-tier claim. Squad size (8) and composition (a 3-man automatic-weapons group + a rifle/bomb-throwing group, per a 'battle platoon' of 3 such squads plus a small HQ) come from Wikipedia's own synthesis of MacKenzie 1995 (the standard academic monograph, not read directly this session) -- the source's own section-vs-platoon terminology is internally ambiguous and not resolved here. weapon1 (M1918A2 BAR): US Lend-Lease automatic rifles (25,000 supplied) were a real, sourced Home Guard weapon by 1943, alongside an unmodeled alternative (Lewis LMG, ~14,000 supplied) -- BAR chosen since it already has sourced RPM data in this roster (weapons.csv) and no Home-Guard-specific split between the two types was found. weapon2 (P17 Enfield): the US-supplied M1917 'P17' rifle (500,000 purchased) was Home Guard's standard rifle by 1943, distinct from the Lee-Enfield used by the Regular Army's own Rifle Section (UK_RIFSEC) -- added as a new weapons.csv row using the same generic bolt-action rifle RPM figures (20 cyclic/15 practical/600yd) already used identically for Kar98k/M1903 Springfield/Mosin-Nagant in this file, since no P17-specific rate-of-fire figure was sourced or expected to differ meaningfully from any other WWI-era bolt-action design. g_number=2 is one below this roster's usual full-squad baseline (G3 for every other Regular rifle squad) -- G# has no formula in this project (every row's value is designer-assigned, see infantry_calc/README.md), and no Home-Guard-specific close-assault/grenade-effectiveness source was found; one step down from the regular-squad baseline is this row's own inference from the Militia tier's lower training level, not a sourced figure. No historical validation data: the Home Guard never fought ground combat (the invasion it was raised against never came) -- its only combat record is anti-aircraft/coastal-gunnery, a different combat mode this project's infantry system doesn't model, so none is claimed here. See counters/toe/militia_tier_validation_1943.md for the full research pass, including two other candidates considered and not recommended (German Volkssturm -- the single most explicit quantified low-training claim found ('10-14 days'), but 13 months outside this project's 1943 window and no sub-battalion TOE found; Soviet opolcheniye -- 2 years outside the window AND the 'militia' designation itself was transitional, divisions redesignated as ordinary Rifle/Guards divisions within weeks to months, so no honestly-dated 1943 opolcheniye unit exists at all).
